## Judgments (vetoable)

**K9 and K10 survive, and they are not equivalent.** The fix's condition is a conjunction: a hole is dropped before the
proofs when the kernel made it under 4 m² **and** the clean leaves it under 4 m². K9 drops the first clause, K10 the
second; both pass the whole folder (87 / 87). `probes/k910.mts` shows the difference on two crafted holes 10 cm off an
outer ring, each a 2 m rectangle with a 15 cm dent or bump on one side (inside Douglas–Peucker's 20 cm):

| hole | made | cleaned | the code | K9 | K10 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A (dent) | 3.93 m² | 4.08 m² | `not clear (rings meet)` | `not clear (rings meet)` | kept 1 ring (the hole dropped) |
| B (bump) | 4.07 m² | 3.92 m² | `not clear (rings meet)` | kept 1 ring (the hole dropped) | `not clear (rings meet)` |

So the three forms differ only for a hole whose area crosses the sliver threshold under the clean — a band a few
per cent wide around 4 m². The round's stated promises are each pinned on both sides of that band: a sub-sliver islet
is dropped (K7, K11), a hole over the sliver area is still proved (K12, at 5 m²), an outer ring is proved whatever its
area (K8, K8b). Which side a band hole falls on is a tightening of the claim, and every form fails safely there (a
typed refusal, or a commit with an islet of about 4 m² under water); nothing persisted depends on it. Under the brief's
blocker rule and N-45 this seat records it as a hardening row (N-s4c-1) and not as a blocker — as the S3 check did for
R1c (accepted J546). **The tally** (`mI`: the tree's sources plus a counting block in `provedRings`; its rows are
equal to `mirror`'s on all 303 runs, so the count changes nothing): over the 303 census runs 143 kernel rings reach
`provedRings` (130 on relief-3000's 128 slow-ring runs, 13 on the bar's 10); the clean empties none; **2 are holes,
both seed 184's, both made and cleaned under 4 m²; 0 holes fall in either band** (made under / cleaned over; made
over / cleaned under), 0 holes are over the sliver area, 0 outer rings are under it. So K9 and K10 are equivalent to
the code on every input met — the same footing as R1c at the S3 check (0 of 10 439 outfalls; accepted J546, and pinned
this round as Q114). The finishing seat re-ran `probes/k910.mts` on `mirror` and reads the same table (A: made 3.93 m²,
cleaned 4.08 m²; B: made 4.07 m², cleaned 3.92 m²; the code refuses both `not clear (rings meet)`).

**Why not a blocker, in this lane's reading of the rule** ("a survivor on a stated promise you do not find equivalent
stays a blocker"): the survivors are not equivalent in principle, and C-0468 words the condition as the conjunction —
so this is stated here as a judgment the session may veto, not settled by a label. What the round promises about the
outcome is pinned on both sides: the sub-sliver islet is dropped and the river commits (K7, K11), a hole over the
sliver area and every outer ring are still proved (K12, K8, K8b). The two clauses split only on which side of 4 m² a
hole within a few per cent of the threshold falls once the clean moves its area — a tightening of a claim under the
brief's rule (3), fail-safe in every form (N-45), on nothing persisted, and met by no input of 303.

Hole B also shows the residue of Q122's own class: a pocket the kernel makes just OVER 4 m² that the clean leaves under
it is still proved before `partsOf` drops it, and refuses the body if it meets another ring. No seed shows it (the
census); it is part of N-s4c-1.
